tool.name: pathotypr classify
tool.description: genotypes assembled genomes against a marker panel
tool.command:
## The sample list is used rather than passing the genomes as files, because it ## carries the sample name in its own column. Derived from the filename instead, ## the summary reports the genome as "[sample1.fasta] sample1"; here the first ## column is the name, so it comes back as "sample1". ## It also pairs each GFF with its genome explicitly rather than by filename. #import re ## The extension is stripped so the reported sample is "sample1" rather than ## "sample1.fasta", and re-added only for the linked filename. #set $safe = lambda s: re.sub('[.](fasta|fa|fna|fas)$', '', re.sub('[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]', '_', str(s))) #for $g in $genomes #set $name = $safe($g.element_identifier) ln -s '$g' '${name}.fasta' && ## A nested loop rather than a lookup built with a generator expression: ## Cheetah rewrites a generator's loop variable into a function call, and the ## Python it emits then refuses to compile. #set $gff = None #if $annotation.use_gff == 'yes' #for $f in $annotation.gff_files #if $safe($f.element_identifier) == $name #set $gff = $f #end if #end for #end if #if $gff is not None ln -s '$gff' '${name}.gff' && printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' '$name' '${name}.fasta' '${name}.gff' >> samples.tsv && #else printf '%s\t%s\n' '$name' '${name}.fasta' >> samples.tsv && #end if #end for
pathotypr classify --markers '$markers' --reference '$reference' --input-list samples.tsv --output-prefix 'result' --kmer-size $kmer_size --min-flank-bases $min_flank_bases $nested_classification $output_masked_fasta @THREADS@

param.name: genomes
param.label: Assembled genomes
param.help: One or more FASTA assemblies to genotype.

param.name: gff_files
param.label: GFF annotation
param.help: Paired with each genome by element name, so a GFF must be named like its genome.

param.label: Minimum flanking bases
param.help: Bases required on each side of the allele inside the marker k-mer. At the defaults this caps usable alleles at 11 bp.

param.label: Also write masked FASTA
param.help: Writes each genome with the marker positions replaced by N.

tool.help:
**What it does**
`pathotypr classify` calls a panel of diagnostic variants directly on assembled genomes. For each marker it builds a k-mer centred on the variant, looks for it in the assembly, and reports which allele was found. Hits are then collapsed into a lineage call per genome.
It produces two tables:
- **per-marker hits**: one row per marker found, with the k-mer, its position, the reference and alternate alleles, the lineage the marker belongs to and, where the panel carries them, the gene and amino-acid change. - **summary**: one row per genome, with the count of hits per lineage and the major lineage call.
@MARKER_HELP@
@ORGANISM_NOTE@
**Choosing between classify and split-fastq**
Use this tool when you have assemblies. Use *pathotypr split-fastq* when you have raw reads and would rather not assemble them. Both read the same panel and agree on the call; only the input differs.
